svg.title: Feedforward: the volts physics says you need
svg.desc: Animated, two graphs drawn left to right together. Top: the dashed setpoint speed ramps up and holds; the solid orange measured speed follows it closely, a few percent low, and then closes the last bit. Bottom: the volts. The moment the setpoint starts to move, a large gray area, feedforward, jumps up with it, before any error appears; it carries most of the volts. A thin blue sliver on top, feedback (PID), only adds the little left over. The green line is the total. Footer: V = kS·sgn(v) + kV·v + kA·a: a little to get going, more the faster it spins, more again to speed up.
svg.text: Feedforward: the volts physics says you need
Sent right away, from the setpoint, before any error appears.

g.text: setpoint moves: feedforward answers at once

svg.text: V = kS·sgn(v) + kV·v + kA·a: a little to get going (kS), more the faster
it spins (kV), more again to speed up (kA). With a measured feedforward a
drive wheel is within a few percent of its target before PID does anything.
It uses the setpoint, not the measurement: it answers before the question.
